newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM Deve Gowda departs for Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM Deve Gowda departs for Moscow.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda left on Monday for a three-day official visit to Russia to strengthen bilateral ties, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
Deve Gowda was accompanied by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah.
Deve Gowda will hold talks with Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Tuesday, PTI said.

India and Russia are expected to sign several agreements on subjects such as double taxation, customs cooperation, extradition of criminals, mutual legal assistance in criminal affairs and consular convention, it added.
Deve Gowda told reporters before departing for Moscow that the entire gamut of bilateral relations with Russia would be covered in his talks with Yeltsin and other leaders, PTI said.
The issues of private participation in the power sector, Afghanistan and the proposed sale of Russian nuclear reactors to India would also be raised, Indian officials said.
Government officials were unavailable to comment due to a national holiday in India.
